answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a small, nontransferable bond before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation updates. After a completed task, randomly selected counterparties verify the result; proven fraud burns the bond and removes that identity’s weight, while honest agents recover it. Creating a hollow grove of umber-named accounts therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing each bond when those accounts misbehave.
